request.description: Characterize compiled MuJoCo inertia, direct motor torque, and 50 Hz saturated step and impulse responses at inner, middle, and outer official-radius IK configurations on both elbow branches.
request.rationale: The initial decision is whether the complete 1 cm, 2 second hold is plausibly limited by actuator authority and sampled-time stabilization or is more likely a learned-policy and distribution-coverage problem. This learning-independent measurement tests configuration-dependent inertia, acceleration, velocity decay, and end-effector motion at the actual control interval. Slow or strongly branch/radius-dependent responses would prioritize control and precision work; fast, consistent responses would make a baseline policy and stratified official-distribution evaluation the higher-value next direction. The fresh entry point avoids replaying the stale failed M1 module dispatch; the scientific measurement is unchanged.

request.candidates_and_roles: No learned candidates exist yet; working, best-known, and retained roles remain empty.
request.cumulative_resource_use: One completed learning-independent measurement (M2); no training steps or policy-evaluation episodes consumed. M1 was a failed implementation attempt and is superseded execution history, not evidence.
request.current_goal_gap: No learned candidate has been trained or evaluated, so the distance to 98% official success is unmeasured. The remaining actionable gap is to determine whether a policy can exploit the available plant authority across the full target distribution while regulating residual motion during the complete hold.
request.current_synthesis: Observed in M2: the compiled model uses 0.02 s control intervals, 5.0 joint torque at unit control, approximately 0.0102-0.0119 joint mass-matrix diagonal terms across the tested radii, and approximately 421-491 rad/s^2 initial unit-control acceleration. A 25-control-step saturated step reached roughly 9.2-10.0 rad/s joint speed and the post-release joint velocity fell below 0.02 rad/s by control step 30-34. A one-control-step saturated impulse produced up to about 0.040 m end-effector displacement at the outer radius, versus about 0.012 m at the inner radius. Interpretation: gross actuator authority and damping are not the leading hard ceiling for reaching or settling; the plant can become highly sensitive to poorly regulated 20 ms action changes, especially near the outer radius. Competing explanations now are (A) policy/distribution limitation, with failures concentrated in the untrained inner annulus or inconsistent IK branch use, versus (B) learned closed-loop precision limitation, with entry velocity or residual oscillation causing hold interruptions despite adequate plant authority. M2 does not measure a learned policy, action saturation during task behavior, branch consistency, or continuous hold semantics, so it cannot establish which explanation dominates.
request.decision_frontier: Does a baseline learned policy fail primarily because training omits the inner 0.06-0.14 m annulus and leaves branch usage inconsistent, or because the policy cannot regulate entry and hold-phase motion tightly enough at 50 Hz? Discriminating evidence is a full-distribution policy evaluation with radius-angle bins, first-entry step and distance, maximum held steps, interruptions, and branch traces; an inner-radius deficit supports coverage/branch limitation, while all-radius failures with low entry error but repeated hold exits support precision regulation. If failures correlate with action saturation and residual velocity, prioritize control-aware policy design; if failures correlate with radius and branch while stable holds occur when reached, prioritize training coverage and branch-consistent representation.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2 second hold inside the 1 cm tolerance. M2 establishes the plant capability needed to decide whether to prioritize control authority diagnosis or learned-policy and distribution diagnosis before training.
